blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights ROS (Robot Operating System) as an influential open-source framework introduced in 2009, now cited nearly 2000 times and widely adopted (with over 8.5M downloads by 2015). He emphasizes ROS's relevance to distributed systems, noting its peer-to-peer architecture, language-neutral design, and microservices-like philosophy—predating modern trends like event streams and modular services. The blog praises ROS for addressing robotics' unique challenges, such as heterogeneous hardware, large-scale integration, and distributed coordination, while enabling real-time dataflows (e.g., sensor-to-tool transformations). Colyer also underscores ROS's modular toolchain, thin executables, and licensing flexibility, which allows mixing GPL, BSD, and proprietary components without contamination.
paper_title: ROS: an open-source Robot Operating System
